facts.text: Der Rosenkavalier premiered in Dresden on 26 January 1911 and was a triumph from the start; tickets reportedly sold out almost immediately.
evidence: Der Rosenkavalier premiered on 26 January 1911 in Dresden
From the start, Der Rosenkavalier was nothing short of a triumph: tickets to the premiere reportedly sold out almost immediately

facts.text: Until the premiere the working title was “Ochs auf Lerchenau”. “Ochs” means “ox”, which describes the Baron’s manners.
evidence: Until the premiere, the working title was Ochs auf Lerchenau
"Ochs" means "ox", which describes the Baron's manner

facts.text: Strauss filled the score with Viennese waltzes, an anachronism: the story is set in the 1740s, before the waltz was famous in Vienna.
evidence: This is anachronistic because the story takes place in the 1740s, and the waltz only became famous in Vienna during the early 19th century.

facts.text: Some critics objected to the anachronistic waltzes, but the public embraced the opera unconditionally.
facts.evidence: Though some critics took issue with Strauss's anachronistic use of waltz music, the public embraced the opera unconditionally.

facts.text: Alfred Roller designed the original sets and costumes, and Strauss and Hofmannsthal had his designs published in a prompt book that all productions had to use.
evidence: Strauss and Hofmannsthal commissioned Roller to design sets and costumes for Der Rosenkavalier
published in an illustrated prompt book that all productions would be obligated to use

facts.text: Max Reinhardt was quietly brought in to help with rehearsals as a “shadow director”, though Georg Toller remained the only credited director.
facts.evidence: recruited Max Reinhardt to assist with rehearsals as a "shadow director"

facts.text: The opera showcases the female voice: Sophie, Octavian and the Marschallin are all sung by women, who share a trio at the opera’s emotional climax.
evidence: Der Rosenkavalier is notable for showcasing the female voice
who share several duets as well as a trio at the opera's emotional climax

facts.text: Some singers have performed two or even all three of the leading female roles over their careers.
facts.evidence: Some singers have performed two or even all three of these roles over the course of their careers.

facts.text: The Met gave the opera’s US premiere on 9 December 1913, conducted by Alfred Hertz.
facts.evidence: The United States premiere took place at the Metropolitan Opera on the following 9 December in a production conducted by Alfred Hertz.

facts.text: Within two months of its premiere it was translated into Italian and performed at La Scala.
facts.evidence: Within two months of its premiere, the work was translated into Italian and performed at La Scala.

facts.text: In the Marschallin’s reverie on the passing of time, a clock is heard chiming 13 times.
facts.evidence: a clock is heard chiming 13 times

facts.text: Strauss and Hofmannsthal mark social class through language: Octavian’s “Mariandl” and other non-noble characters speak an Austrian dialect.
facts.evidence: The language used by Octavian as Mariandl, and by other non-noble characters, is an Austrian dialect
